evidence.note: Assessed the large coupled scope and decided to start with foundational data-model methods before algorithm-heavy pieces — dependency awareness at the outset.
Tackled analysis first, explicitly because it was 'simpler' than parity; used cargo test --test analysis_tests as the completion signal for that grouping.
Moved to CLI commands as a coherent grouping and used cli_tests pass/fail as the done-check (50/51 passing) before advancing.
Recognized parity tests were blocked by todo!() in runners.rs and sequenced implementing runners.rs to unblock the parity test group — dependency-aware unblocking.

Deferred harder components (BIF serialization, alignment merge) to later, tackling NOA/EDA before BIF, and alignment last; but handled newly-revealed alignment coupling reactively rather than revising an explicit plan.
Final tally reported per test group (CLI/lib/analysis/parity/pipeline), reflecting that milestones were organized by test suite throughout.

reasoning: The agent consistently grouped work by component/test suite and progressed in a sensible dependency order (model → parsers → analysis → alignment → layout → CLI → parity runners), each grouping closed by a runnable test group as its done-check — squarely matching anchor 5, with the extra dependency reasoning (choosing 'simpler/foundational' groupings first and unblocking parity via runners.rs) pushing above it. It falls short of 8 because there was no explicit upfront milestone plan defining each milestone by a predefined test set; the sequencing was emergent and the numerous 'Plan:' lines were mostly tactical navigation, and coupling discoveries were handled reactively rather than through plan revision. Hence a 6.
